title: Prompt-preserve regression orchard: measuring semantic drift from batching + prefix-cache compression
creator: Aisha Khan
description:
Goal: quantify semantic drift and token-level coherence regressions introduced by changes to batching and prefix/KV cache compression policies. This ticket builds a reproducible eval harness that runs A/B comparisons between baseline config and a change (e.g., larger microbatch size, compressed kvcache entries, prefix merge heuristics). The focus is on subtle quality degradations that do not show up in token-perplexity but cause downstream semantic inconsistencies (hallucination, truncated completions, instruction-following lapses).

Background: recent rollout candidates for optimistic microbatch scaling and an experimental kvcache packing mode produced indistinct latency wins in internal benchmarks but raised early QA notes about occasional answer truncation and instruction-ignoring failures for long-context prompts. Current smoke tests (BLEU/ROUGE/perplexity) are insufficient. We need an operationalizable suite that: (1) exercises real prompt distributions (chat + instruction + multi-turn), (2) isolates batching vs cache effects, (3) surfaces regressions with prioritized signal for rollback policies.

Deliverables: harness code on GH with reproducible notebook, canonical prompt corpus (stratified by turn-length and tokenization boundary stresscases), evaluation metrics (semantic equivalence score, instruction-following pass rate, answer-completeness), dashboard prototype in Console, and a recommended gating rule for rollout (e.g., no >0.6% delta on instruction-follow pass rate on production-weighted slice).
acceptance_criteria: A portable harness that can run pairwise config comparisons across baseline and candidate on a sampled prompt corpus
A metric suite including at least: semantic-equivalence (embedding cosine + threshold), instruction-following binary pass, completion-truncation rate, and latency distribution by percentile
Dashboard that visualizes per-slice deltas (by prompt-length, model, and customer-weight) and flags slices that exceed thresholds
A documented rollback/gating recommendation for Canary and auto-fallback policies
Repro script and one recorded run comparing: baseline (microbatch=4, kvcache: uncompressed) vs candidate (microbatch=12, kvcache: packed-compressed) with results in GH artifact link
steps: Assemble stratified prompt corpus: sample 10k prompts from production traces, anonymize, and label by slice (short/system-instruction/long-multi-turn/token-boundary-stress)
Implement harness runner that spawns controlled traffic simulators to the runtime with toggled config overrides (use low-rate to avoid impacting prod) and records token-level traces and latencies
Integrate semantic-equivalence comparator using model-embeddings (redwood-embed-1) and a calibrated threshold per-slice
Add wrapper to detect truncation by comparing expected vs emitted completion lengths and semantic divergence near end-of-output
Create a lightweight Console dashboard prototype with per-slice delta heatmap and downloadable artifacts
Run full comparison on GPU staging with both small and large models; produce artifact and draft PR with results
